title: SDK Boot-to-Production Accelerator and Support Checklist
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page is an end-to-end accelerator for taking a Redwood SDK integration from first commit to stable production usage. It combines: reusable quickstart templates, API examples (safe defaults), docs-site publishing guidance, telemetry assertions, and a compact support checklist with canonical fixes for the most common problems our support and DX teams see. Use this as the canonical preflight and first-line support reference when working with teams shipping SDK-based features.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-prod-call to under 4 hours for small sample apps.
- Establish a minimal set of telemetry and assertions so regressions are caught in CI or the first hour after rollout.
- Provide a reproducible support triage that yields fixes or escalations within 60 minutes for 80% of incidents.

Scope
- Applies to: JS/TypeScript and Python SDKs, client-side integrations (server-to-server), and edge adapters.
- Does NOT cover: on-prem runtime packaging (see eng-private-deployments), custom quantization and kernel changes (see eng-serving-runtime).

Quickstart Accelerator (Templates and Commands)

1) Repository layout (recommended)
- /examples/simple-app/ -> minimal runnable sample (local env + docker-compose)
- /templates/sdk-wrapper/ -> small adapter with credential rotation hooks
- /ci/ -> preflight checks and telemetry assertions

2) Minimal local dev steps (copy-paste)
1. Install: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk || pip install redwood-sdk
2. Export key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=rc_test_XXXXXXXX
3. Run sample: node examples/simple-app/index.js or python examples/simple-app/app.py
4. Smoke test: curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-v1","input":"hello"}'

3) Standard config file (example)
| key | recommended | notes |
|-----|-------------|-------|
| model | rwd-small-v1 | pick model from catalog; pin exact version in prod |
| timeout_ms | 12000 | client-side hard timeout for generation requests |
| stream | true | enable streaming only if front-end supports incremental tokens |
| max_concurrency | 8 | per-process concurrency guard to avoid local connection storms |
| telemetry_context | service=payments,team=checkout | three tags: service, team, environment |

API Example Patterns (safe defaults)
- Use idempotency keys for multi-token operations (e.g., batch generation) to avoid double-charges and duplicated outputs. Pattern: X-Idempotency-Key: sha256(user_id|prompt_hash|timestamp-window).
- Retry policy (recommended): exponential-backoff with jitter; max attempts=4; non-idempotent ops should use 0 retries from client.
- Streaming: fallback to chunked polling if the client cannot handle partial events; treat non-delivery as a transient network issue and retry whole request once.

Docs-site & Quickstart Publishing Guidelines
- Quickstarts must include: one-liner, runnable snippet, expected output, failure modes, and how to inspect telemetry.
- Publish flow: author -> internal review (1 reviewer) -> staging preview (docs site) -> smoke test runner -> publish. Each step must be completed within the PR description.
- Staging checks (CI job names): docs:build, docs:preview, examples:smoke. Failure of any check blocks publish.

Telemetry and Preflight Assertions (must be in CI)
- Required metrics (minimum): request_count, success_rate, latency_ms_p95, token_count.
- Required traces: one end-to-end trace per smoke test that includes client->gateway->runtime spans with these attributes: model, model_version, shard_id, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size.
- CI assertions (examples):
  - request_count > 0 after smoke test
  - success_rate >= 0.98
  - latency_ms_p95 <= 1000ms for small payloads (<=128 tokens)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.2 for repeated-prefix tests

Support Triaging Runbook (first 60 minutes)
1) Gather context (owner/SDR)
- Client request ID (X-Request-Id or dev-provided idempotency key)
- Timestamp and region
- SDK version and pinned model/version
- Logs: client logs, gateway request logs, runtime request trace id

2) Reproduce locally (fast path)
- Use the sample app in /examples/simple-app on developer machine with same SDK version and model pins.
- Run the curl smoke test above and attach --verbose output.

3) Check observability (ordered)
- Dashboard: per-tenant latency and error rate (Console -> Observability -> tenant/<tenant-id>)
- Traces: link request id to trace (Search by X-Request-Id)
- Runtime metrics: GPU util, queue_depth, batch_latency (Grafana dashboards: runtime/pool-<region>)

4) Common immediate root causes and canonical fixes
- Auth fail (401)
  - Symptom: immediate 401 in client logs, no runtime traces.
  - Fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, check token rotation logs, re-issue token via console or Secrets manager, invalidate old tokens.
- Model mismatch / incompatible schema (400)
  - Symptom: 400 with payload schema error; runtime shows decode exception.
  - Fix: pin model_version to a known-compatible tag; convert payload to canonical JSON schema; run local schema validator.
- Thundering retries / fanout (5xx spikes)
  - Symptom: rapid spike in 5xxs and rising queue_depth; high batch_latency.
  - Fix: apply client-side concurrency limits (max_concurrency), add exponential backoff; temporarily enable rate-limiter in gateway for offending tenant.
- KV cache invalidation / cold-cache thrash (high latency)
  - Symptom: p95 latency increases after new prompt distributions; kv_cache_hit_rate drops towards 0.
  - Fix: for canary traffic, seed cache with representative prefixes (telemetry-backed), or temporarily reduce batch_size to reduce miss amplification.
- Token accounting mismatch / billing discrepancies
  - Symptom: user reports unexpected cost delta; telemetry shows sudden token_count deviation.
  - Fix: reconcile SDK client-side tokenization version; pin tokenizer or upgrade both client and server tokenizers; file ticket to billing.

Escalation Matrix
- Level 0 (Owner): DX engineer + customer engineer — handle auth and simple schema fixes, telemetry missing. Response target: 30 minutes.
- Level 1 (Runtime): serving-runtime oncall — performance regressions (p95 latency > 3x baseline), queue_depth persistently > 80%. Response target: 60 minutes.
- Level 2 (SRE/Infra): capacity and networking incidents — loss of region capacity, routing failures. Response target: 120 minutes.

Templates: Support Reply Snippets (copy-paste)
- Short acknowledgement: "Thanks — we received your trace id: {{trace_id}}. We've confirmed an elevated error rate and are investigating. ETA 60 minutes."
- Temporary mitigation: "We've enabled a 20rps tenant throttle and pinned model to {{model_version}} while we root cause. You may see degraded throughput for 10–20 minutes."

Postmortem & Regression Prevention Checklist (if incident > 30m)
- Create postmortem within 72 hours (contributor, reviewer, owner).
- Add at least one automated CI assertion that would have caught the regression. Examples: latency_p95 threshold, kv_cache_hit_rate assertion, or token_count delta test.
- If fix involved config change, capture it as a default in the SDK quickstart template or a recommended runtime flag.

Operational Notes for DX Team
- Keep a small set of golden traces per SDK version and model (store trace ids in examples/golden-traces.json).
- Weekly health check job: smoke tests across regions every 4 hours; fail if success_rate < 0.99 for 2 consecutive runs.
- Ownership: maintainers for the quickstart templates are listed in CODEOWNERS under /examples/. Keep that file updated.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and validators
- Schema validator (node): npx @redwood-inference/schema-validate ./payloads/sample.json --model rwd-small-v1
- Trace query (curl): curl -sS "https://internal-observability.redwood/api/traces?trace_id={{trace_id}}" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OBS_API_KEY'
- Local concurrency guard (bash): 
  export MAX_CONCURRENCY=8
  for i in $(seq 1 $MAX_CONCURRENCY); do node examples/simple-app/index.js & done

Contact & Ownership
- DX primary: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example.com)
- Runtime oncall: see oncall rota (eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki)
- Support escalation Slack channel: #dx-runtime-escalations

Change log
- 2026-02-10: created initial boot-to-prod accelerator and checklist.
- 2026-07-18: updated telemetry assertions (added kv_cache_hit_rate) and added canonical fixes for billing/token mismatches.

End of document.
